summary: This bill creates a federal grant program, administered by the Attorney General, that funds states, localities, and tribes to develop and run handgun purchaser licensing systems requiring applicants to be at least 21, submit fingerprints and pass background checks, and renew permits every five years.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates a new federal grant program under the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act, authorizing 'such sums as may be necessary' for states and localities to develop and run handgun purchaser licensing systems. This directly expands federal spending on a new initiative.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
The bill has no provisions addressing healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.

The core purpose of the bill is to fund and incentivize state-level handgun purchaser licensing regimes that impose age minimums, background checks, fingerprinting, periodic renewal, and disqualification for prohibited persons. This is a direct effort to impose stricter gun regulations.
The bill references immigration status only to define eligibility for a handgun license (citizen, national, or lawful permanent resident). This is incidental and does not alter immigration policy.
The bill has no provisions related to abortion or reproductive rights.
The bill does not address military or defense spending.
The bill has no provisions related to environmental regulation or climate policy.
The bill has no provisions related to welfare programs or social safety-net benefits.
The bill has no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill has no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.

While the bill uses criminal background checks as part of licensing, its primary focus is gun regulation rather than broader criminal-justice reforms such as sentencing, policing practices, or rehabilitation.
The bill has no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill authorizes new spending without offsetting cuts or revenue measures, but the fiscal impact is secondary to its regulatory purpose and not framed as a debt-reduction or deficit policy.
The bill has no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
The bill has no provisions related to foreign aid.
The bill has no provisions related to voting access or election administration.
The bill requires fingerprinting and photographs for licensing but does not regulate technology companies or establish broader privacy rules.
The bill has no provisions related to labor unions or worker protections.
The bill has no provisions addressing religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
